newsitem.title: SPAIN: Aznar vows to intensify fight against ETA.
newsitem.headline: Aznar vows to intensify fight against ETA.

text.p: Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar vowed on Monday to step up the fight against Basque separatist guerrillas after the killing of a young Spanish politician, pledging "we will put a stop to terrorism."

But, in his first public comments since the death on Sunday of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, Aznar warned the Spanish people in a nationally televised address of "painful days" ahead in the struggle against the rebel group ETA.

Blanco, a Basque town councillor, was found on Saturday bound and bloodied, two bullets lodged in his brain, about 48 hours after ETA guerrillas kidnapped him. He died early on Sunday in a hospital in the Basque city of San Sebastian.
"Those who only know how to kill, those who only know how to kidnap, will continue doing it," Aznar said from the steps of government house in Madrid.
But he urged Spaniards to maintain solidarity. "Without a doubt, we're going to win. Without a doubt, we will put a stop to terrorism," he promised.
Aznar also lashed out angrily against ETA's political arm, Herri Batasuna, calling them "accomplices" to murder and urging Spaniards to isolate them.
